links.outcome: Reading grade level of GPT-4 IR procedural instructions versus radiologyinfo.org
links.effect: Flesch-Kincaid grade 7.8 ± 0.87 for GPT-4 vs 9.6 ± 0.83 for radiologyinfo.org (P = .007); Gunning Fog 10.4 vs 12.7; Flesch Reading Ease 69.4 vs 51.3.
links.quote: The readability assessment across all procedural instructions showed a better Flesch-Kincaid mean grade of GPT-4 instructions compared with radiologyinfo.org (7.8 ± 0.87 versus 9.6 ± 0.83; P = .007) indicating excellent readability at 7th- to 8th-grade level compared with 9th to 10th grade.

links.outcome: Clinical appropriateness of GPT-4 patient instructions rated by four physicians
links.effect: Nine of ten GPT-generated instructions were fully appropriate; arterial embolization instructions were only somewhat appropriate.
links.quote: Evaluation by four clinical physicians shows that nine GPT-generated instructions were fully appropriate, whereas arterial embolization instructions was somewhat appropriate.

screen.reason: Evaluates the feasibility, readability, and clinical appropriateness of GPT-4 generated patient educational materials for interventional radiology compared to standard online materials, but does not test a specific deployment safeguard or operational practice.
